title: Understand the Sorter Sweeper Database “single record” constraint during database overview
summary: Use the Sorter Sweeper Database Overview constraint statement (“but there can be only one record yet”) to interpret what the overview is showing when it is expected to be constrained to a single record rather than multiple rows/entries.
when_to_use: When interpreting a Sorter Sweeper Database Overview that is described as having a single-record constraint (“but there can be only one record yet”).
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Interpret the overview content using the single-record constraint statement and capture any mismatch between the expected single-record view and what is observed.
access_or_tools_needed: Training video playback or the captured slide frame artifact for the “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” segment
Access to the live Sorter Sweeper database overview view described by the training segment (exact live tool/screen not specified in the provided packet)

visual_references.description: Slide frame titled “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” with transcript phrase “but there can be only one record yet.”

steps.title: Locate the Sorter Sweeper Database Overview content and confirm the single-record statement
steps.purpose: Ground the interpretation in the exact constraint phrase used during the Sorter Sweeper Database Overview discussion.
steps.instruction: Open the captured slide frame for the “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” segment and confirm the spoken/transcript phrase “but there can be only one record yet.”
steps.expected_result: You have identified the “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” slide frame and the transcript phrase “but there can be only one record yet.”
steps.healthy_condition: The slide frame shows the title “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” and the nearby transcript/OCR includes “but there can be only one record yet.”
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” slide frame or the transcript phrase “but there can be only one record yet” is not present/confirmable.

actions.label: Verify slide title and transcript phrase
actions.exact_action: Confirm the slide frame titled “Sorter Sweeper Database Overview” and the transcript says “but there can be only one record yet.”

steps.title: Interpret the live database overview using the single-record constraint
steps.purpose: Avoid confusion when the live overview is constrained to a single record/entry.
steps.instruction: When viewing the corresponding live database overview (if applicable), interpret the display as constrained to a single record rather than multiple rows/entries.
steps.expected_result: The live overview is interpreted as a single-record constrained view (i.e., you do not expect multiple records/entries if the overview is in the “single record yet” state).
steps.healthy_condition: The live overview shows only one record/entry consistent with the “but there can be only one record yet” constraint.
steps.failure_condition: The live view shows multiple records/entries, which conflicts with the single-record expectation.

actions.label: Compare live overview record count to single-record expectation
actions.exact_action: Check how many records/entries are visible in the live Sorter Sweeper Database Overview and interpret it as single-record constrained when only one is shown.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the live system does not align with the “single record” expectation (e.g., multiple records are present), stop and escalate to deeper support with the observed count/entries.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript phrase used to describe the constraint: "but there can be only one record yet."

steps.title: Capture and escalate any mismatch between expected single-record view and observed multiple records
steps.purpose: Ensure deeper support can investigate why the live overview is not constrained to a single record.
steps.instruction: If the live view shows multiple records/entries, capture the observed number of records/entries visible and escalate for deeper support.
steps.expected_result: You have recorded the observed record/entry count from the live overview and escalated due to mismatch with the single-record expectation.
steps.healthy_condition: Observed record/entry count is consistent with a single-record constrained view (no escalation needed).
steps.failure_condition: Observed record/entry count is greater than one, and escalation is not performed.

actions.label: Record observed count and escalate
actions.exact_action: Capture what is shown (e.g., number of records/entries visible) for follow-up when multiple records are present.

stop_or_escalate_if: Multiple records/entries visible in the live overview when the constraint indicates “only one record yet.”

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Single-record constraint statement: "but there can be only one record yet."

success_criteria: The support agent correctly interprets the overview as single-record constrained when only one record/entry is shown.
If multiple records/entries are shown, the agent captures the observed count/entries and escalates.
healthy_conditions: Live overview shows one record/entry consistent with the “but there can be only one record yet” constraint.
failure_conditions: Live overview shows multiple records/entries despite the single-record constraint expectation.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to deeper support when the live overview shows multiple records/entries; include the observed number of records/entries visible.
